item.title: Harvey Weinstein sentenced to 15 years in New York sexual assault case
item.description: Harvey Weinstein, the disgraced movie mogul, was sentenced to 15 years in prison Wednesday morning for sexually assaulting Miriam Haley at his Manhattan apartment in 2006.

item.title: Notorious hacking group claims it breached FBI services
item.description: The notorious hacking group ShinyHunters claims it breached the FBI's job website. CBS News' Anna Schecter has more.

item.title: 6 people killed in bear attacks in Siberia: "Under siege"
item.description: Prosecutors said they opened a probe into criminal negligence, accusing local officials of failing to control bear numbers.

item.title: U.S., Iran hold first talks since June as Trump threatens annihilation
item.description: U.S. and Iranian delegations met on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly, rekindling diplomacy amid Trump's threat to "annihilate" the regime.

item.title: DOJ defends Trump media ban, citing national security and "professionalism"
item.description: The Justice Department claimed that reporting from CNN, MS NOW and Politico raises national security concerns and accused their journalists of failing to act with "professionalism and decorum."

item.title: The U.S. has 17,500 refugee slots. Trump says they will primarily go to white South Africans.
item.description: The Trump administration says it will allow up to 17,500 refugees to migrate to the U.S. in 2027, despite closing most of the U.S. refugee program, which is meant for those fleeing persecution and violence abroad. President Trump says those refugee spots will "primarily" go to white Afrikaners, who he claims are oppressed. CBS News' Camilo Montoya-Galvez reports.

item.title: Republican senators push for probe into Donald Trump Jr. and Hunter Biden
item.description: Some Republican senators want an investigation into the business dealings of both Donald Trump Jr. and Hunter Biden. CBS News' Nancy Cordes explains why.

item.title: Trump's legal fight to block some journalists from covering him
item.description: President Trump has barred journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico from entering the White House grounds. CBS News legal contributor Katrina Kaufman explains more.

item.title: Zibby Owens on starting over and not silencing your inner voice
item.description: Zibby Owens sits down with "CBS Mornings" to discuss her new book "Between Chapters: How I Started Over, Took Some Chances, and Found the Plot ."

item.title: "Lioness" star Michael Kelly talks season 3 finale
item.description: "Lioness" actor Michael Kelly sits down with "CBS Mornings" to discuss the season 3 finale of the popular series.

item.title: Inside the fight to free Americans locked up in China
item.description: Sylvia Zin has not spoken to her husband, Min Zin, in over 100 days. The American citizen and a scholar, and his wife, say he is being wrongfully detained in China without a trial date. Sylvia spoke with "Face the Nation" moderator Margaret Brennan about her fight to free her husband. Plus, National Committee on U.S.-China Relations president Steve Orlins shares his thoughts.

item.title: Renée Good's family struggles "every day" since she was gunned down by an ICE agent, her mom says
item.description: Family members of people killed by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents testified on Capitol Hill, calling for lawmakers to take action. Renée Good's mother and brother were among them. CBS News' Caitlin Huey-Burns reports.

item.title: Harris supports Abdul El-Sayed campaign; some Republicans break with Trump over gas prices
item.description: Former Vice President Kamala Harris campaigned with Michigan Senate nominee Dr. Abdul El-Sayed. Meanwhile, some Republicans are breaking with President Trump over soaring gas prices. CBS News' Fin Gómez reports.

item.title: These GOP candidates in tight races are calling for a quick end to Iran war
item.description: Some Trump-aligned candidates are calling for an end to the Iran war, even as Trump stands by his Iran strategy and has suggested escalation is possible.

item.title: Chris Spatola, basketball analyst and Mike Krzyzewski's son-in-law, dies at 47
item.description: Spatola played basketball for the U.S. Military Academy and later coached on legendary Duke head coach Mike Krzyzewski's staff.

item.title: Israeli ambassador to the U.N. on Iran, Gaza and U.S. relations as Middle East conflicts heat up
item.description: Danny Danon, the Israeli ambassador to the United Nations, comments on U.S.-Israeli relations, Gaza and the war in Iran.

item.title: Trump rails against Iran, prepares for China's Xi as world concerns about AI explode
item.description: CBS News' Olivia Rinaldi has what you should know about the first day of the United Nations General Assembly and looks ahead to President Trump's meetings with world leaders.

item.title: El Niño could cause 451,000 more heat deaths compared to normal year, group says
item.description: Researchers project nearly half a million more heat-related deaths from June 2026 to February 2027 compared with a typical year, as a result of El Niño.

item.title: Hurricane Polo is a powerful Category 4 storm off Mexico. See its path.
item.description: Hurricane Polo intensified rapidly in the Pacific off the southwestern Mexican coast, growing into a Category 5 storm before weakening slightly to a Category 4. Here's the latest on its path.

item.title: Dolly Parton's estate in feud with her nephew
item.description: Dolly Parton's estate has accused her nephew, Bryan Seaver, of extortion. Seaver, who announced the singer's death last month, was also fired as her head of security. Adriana Diaz reports.

item.title: Exclusive discounts from CBS Mornings Deals
item.description: On this edition of CBS Deals, we show you items that could help improve your everyday lifestyle. Visit cbsdeals.com to take advantage of these exclusive deals today. CBS earns commissions on purchases made through cbsdeals.com.

item.title: Tips for taking care of your life insurance
item.description: Nearly 47% of American households say they feel financial hardship after a primary wage earner dies, according to a recent survey, which is where life insurance comes in. Jill Schlesinger joins with more.

item.title: Meta's Muse shopping agent is a hit, as AI commerce starts to take off
item.description: Meta's new AI tool now ranks at the top of the App Store. Some retail experts see a "natural evolution from search."

item.title: Should the U.S. raise payroll taxes to save Social Security?
item.description: Raising payroll taxes enough to stabilize Social Security could add thousands of dollars in annual costs, according to one analysis.

item.title: Shipwreck, apparent human remains found 7 years after boat sank in Atlantic
item.description: The nonprofit Green Oceans asked the Coast Guard to reopen an investigation that had classified the F/V Mistress as lost.

item.title: Iranian dissident reacts to Trump's promise to either annihilate Iran or make a post-election deal
item.description: CBS News' Ed O'Keefe reports on President Trump's remarks at the United Nations, and Iranian-American activist and journalist Masih Alinejad shares her thoughts on Mr. Trump's war in the Middle East and the plight of the Iranian people.

item.title: Wife of scholar detained in China wants Trump to press Xi to release him
item.description: Min Zin, a Myanmar scholar, has been held for more than 100 days at what human rights groups say is a "black site" in China.

item.title: Norah O'Donnell: Here's what my DEXA scan says about my bone density
item.description: Norah O'Donnell shared what her Dual-Energy X-ray Absorptiometry, or DEXA, scan results were with Dr. Jocelyn Wittstein, who explained what it said about her bone density. Wittstein also asked O'Donnell what her worst health habit was.

item.title: Police officer wounded in shooting near Ontario synagogue on Yom Kippur
item.description: Officials in Canada condemned the shooting and expressed support for law enforcement and the Jewish community.

item.title: Elie Wiesel's son on Trump's U.N. speech, rise of antisemitism in U.S.
item.description: Elisha Wiesel, the son of Nobel Peace Prize laureate and Holocaust survivor Elie Wiesel, joined CBS News to talk about what he wanted to hear from President Trump in his U.N. General Assembly speech, the rise of antisemitism and more.
